articles.title: Single agent vs multi-agent: when subagents are worth it
articles.excerpt: Single agent vs multi-agent is a trade-off between one shared context and several isolated ones. For many production setups in late 2026, Anthropic's Applied AI team now recommends defaulting to one a…
articles.body: Single agent vs multi-agent is a trade-off between one shared context and several isolated ones. For many production setups in late 2026, Anthropic's Applied AI team now recommends defaulting to one agent loop with skills and tools loaded on demand, and keeping a subagent only when evals show it still beats the folded version — or when it truly needs its own context window, parallel runs, or permission isolation. That is the practical answer; the rest of this post is how to decide for your stack. On 22 October 2026 Anthropic published Building agents: When to fold subagents into your main agent loop , arguing that enterprise agents with routers, planners and a subagent per team often lose quality, voice and speed to handoffs and "Frankenprompt" system prompts.

articles.title: Capturing and Searching Application Logs — Python Logging Backend for Media Cohorts
articles.excerpt: A media experiment changes shape when its logs are split across tenant cohorts. The operational constraint is signal quality: a backend that makes every event searchable can still make the experiment…
articles.body: A media experiment changes shape when its logs are split across tenant cohorts. The operational constraint is signal quality: a backend that makes every event searchable can still make the experiment harder to interpret if retries, health checks, and duplicated delivery records swamp the treatment effect. Short answer: choose a log backend by the questions you need to answer, then make the emitted record portable through an open telemetry schema. For cohort analysis, I would first require structured events with stable tenant and experiment fields, a clear timestamp policy, bounded retention, and a query path that can aggregate without turning raw text into the data model. The storage engine is secondary to those contracts. This is the choice I make for a notebook-to-prod workflow.

articles.title: The patch decision is made by the artifact it's checking
articles.excerpt: A spec published on 24 October exists to answer one question: when a patched version of a skill appears, which other versions are still carrying the old bug? The spec is called Skill Derivation Graph,…
articles.body: A spec published on 24 October exists to answer one question: when a patched version of a skill appears, which other versions are still carrying the old bug? The spec is called Skill Derivation Graph, v0.1. It has a good rule for that question. Section 3.3, "Identity", makes derivation a property you compute: two files with the same normalised text have the same hash, so "a copy that records its parent's hash is verbatim if its own hash matches and modified otherwise, so the derivation type is computed rather than declared." The code agrees. skillgraph/hashing.py:51 defines classify_derivation(child_text, parent_hash) . It hashes the child, compares it to the parent hash, returns verbatim or modified . It is exported in skillgraph/__init__.py . It is unit tested twice.

articles.title: TranchePool Exploit: A Midnight Rollover Drained $1.01M
articles.excerpt: Originally published at TranchePool Exploit: A Midnight Rollover Drained $1.01M Shortly after midnight UTC on 28 October 2026, an attacker drained 1,013,353.61 USDC from a TranchePool on Avalanche C-C…
articles.body: Originally published at TranchePool Exploit: A Midnight Rollover Drained $1.01M Shortly after midnight UTC on 28 October 2026 , an attacker drained 1,013,353.61 USDC from a TranchePool on Avalanche C-Chain that SlowMist reports is associated with Valinor Digital, Oatfi and Fence Finance . The pool lost its entire USDC balance. There was no oracle manipulation and no reentrancy. The bug was a piece of credit accounting: when the calendar turned to a new UTC day, the pool treated a scheduled principal repayment as if it had actually been paid, even though no USDC arrived. That single bookkeeping step gave the attacker a fresh line of draw capacity, and the attacker used it three seconds after midnight.

articles.title: Linux Server Feeling Slow? 7 Checks Before You Reboot
articles.excerpt: Linux Server Feeling Slow? 7 Checks Before You Reboot Every sysadmin has been there: 2 AM, an alert fires, the app is crawling, and your first instinct is to reboot the box. Reboots feel like a reset…
articles.body: Linux Server Feeling Slow? 7 Checks Before You Reboot Every sysadmin has been there: 2 AM, an alert fires, the app is crawling, and your first instinct is to reboot the box. Reboots feel like a reset button, and sometimes they work. But they rarely fix the real problem. If a server slows down every Tuesday at the same hour, rebooting it every Tuesday is not a fix — it is a habit. Before you reach for reboot , run these seven checks. They take about five minutes and they will usually tell you what is actually wrong. 1. Load Average vs. CPU: Is It Busy or Blocked? Start with uptime . It gives you the one-minute, five-minute, and fifteen-minute load averages. uptime # 02:14:33 up 41 days, 3:12, 2 users, load average: 18.6, 17.2, 15.9 Now compare the load to your core count with nproc .

articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 28, 1971: Britain launches its 1st satellite Prospero into space on a Black Arrow rocket
articles.excerpt: On Oct. 28, 1971, the United Kingdom launched its first satellite. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Oct. 28, 1971, the United Kingdom launched its first satellite. The satellite was named Prospero, but it was also known as the X-3. This wasn't Britain's first satellite , but it was the first and only one the British space program launched with one of its own rockets. The first six British satellites all launched from the United States on NASA rockets. Prospero launched on a carrier rocket called the Black Arrow. The Prospero mission was the fourth and final flight of a Black Arrow rocket . Prospero was designed to study how the environment in space affects communications satellites. It tested things solar cells and telemetry systems, and even had a micrometeoroid detector that would determine small particles in space posed a threat to the spacecraft.

articles.title: 5 days beneath the waves: What it's like to live in an underwater 'space station'
articles.excerpt: Confined inside a research station 22 feet (7 meters) underwater, Analog Astronaut Commander Dr. Musilova and her crew performed research and maintenance activities like future astronauts on Mars.
articles.body: Living underwater was surprisingly peaceful. It was in many ways exactly what I imagine living on Mars would be like one day. There were no humans around us, except for my three SEA STAR crewmembers and me. Apart from the human noises we made, we couldn't hear anything other than the life support systems keeping us alive submerged 22 feet (7 meters) below the surface. We were living in these extreme conditions to study the challenges astronauts may face on long-duration space missions. Since performing research in space is still rare and expensive, there are numerous facilities around the world that focus on recreating space-like conditions on Earth . One of those stations is the Jules' Undersea Lab, where the SEA STAR simulated space mission took place.

articles.title: ISS astronaut will conduct Canada's 1st spacewalk in 7 years on Oct. 29: Watch it live
articles.excerpt: Joshua Kutryk will venture outside the International Space Station on Oct. 29, on the first spacewalk by a Canadian astronaut in more than seven years. Here's how to watch it live.
articles.body: The next International Space Station (ISS) spacewalk will have more maple-leaf flavor than usual, as a Canadian astronaut will become the first to go outside the orbiting complex in seven years. Canadian Space Agency (CSA) astronaut Joshua Kutryk, who's also a colonel in the Royal Canadian Air Force, will help the ISS boost its power supply during his first-ever spacewalk on Thursday (Oct. 29). Kutryk will be joined by NASA astronaut Anil Menon, who has done three spacewalks already and also serves as a colonel with the U.S. Space Force . The duo are scheduled to venture outside the orbiting lab at 8 a.m. EDT (1200 GMT), kicking off a spacewalk that will last roughly 6 hours and 45 minutes. articles.title: Meet Apeiron, Virgin Galactic's 1st 'Delta-class' space plane
articles.excerpt: Virgin Galactic has officially unveiled its first "Delta-class" space plane, and announced the results of the worldwide vote to choose its name.
articles.body: Virgin Galactic has officially unveiled the first space plane in its next-gen "Delta" line, and announced the results of the worldwide vote to choose its name. Spaceship Apeiron will be the first Delta-class vehicle, Virgin Galactic revealed on Wednesday (Oct. 28). Apeiron (pronounced "A'-per-on," according to the announcement) takes its name from the ancient Greek word meaning "boundless," and was selected through a public poll that drew votes from thousands of people across 83 countries and six continents. The reveal comes on the same day that the space plane is scheduled to be flown from its manufacturing facility in Mesa, Arizona, to Spaceport America in New Mexico, where the vehicle will undergo final preparations before beginning flight tests.
